```python
"""NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory (added by Offramp).

Token Factory is OpenAI-compatible: migrated call sites use the OpenAI SDK
with the client below. Nemotron reasons by default, so every call passes
extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": <bool>}}.
"""

import os

from openai import OpenAI

NEBIUS_BASE_URL = "https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1"

# Nemotron tiers on Token Factory, cheapest first (ids from GET /v1/models).
LIGHTNING = "nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning"
SUPER = "nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b"
ULTRA = "nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b"


def token_factory_client() -> OpenAI:
    """Token Factory client: reads NEBIUS_API_KEY (and NEBIUS_BASE_URL)."""
    return OpenAI(
        api_key=os.environ["NEBIUS_API_KEY"],
        base_url=os.environ.get("NEBIUS_BASE_URL", NEBIUS_BASE_URL),
    )
```

```python
"""Pull structured order and customer fields out of a customer email."""

import json
from typing import Literal

from anthropic import Anthropic
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class OrderFields(BaseModel):
    order_id: str | None = Field(description="Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated")
    customer_name: str | None = Field(description="Full name of the customer as written")
    customer_email: str | None = Field(description="Customer's email address")
    order_date: str | None = Field(description="Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated")
    total_amount: float | None = Field(description="Order total as a plain number, no symbol")
    currency: str | None = Field(description="ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR")
    issue: Literal[
        "damaged", "missing_item", "wrong_item", "late_delivery", "billing_error", "other"
    ]


ORDER_SCHEMA = OrderFields.model_json_schema()

EXTRACT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You extract structured order data from customer support emails.
Reply with a single JSON object that validates against the JSON schema given in the user message.
Use null for any field the email does not state; never guess.
Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD, currencies as ISO 4217 codes, and amounts as plain numbers with a dot
as the decimal separator. Keep names exactly as written. The email may be in any language.
Do not wrap the JSON in markdown and do not add any commentary."""


class ExtractionError(ValueError):
    """The model's reply was not a JSON object matching `OrderFields`."""


def parse_order_fields(text: str) -> OrderFields:
    start, end = text.find("{"), text.rfind("}")
    if start == -1 or end < start:
        raise ExtractionError(f"no JSON object in model reply: {text[:80]!r}")
    try:
        return OrderFields.model_validate_json(text[start : end + 1])
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise ExtractionError(str(exc)) from exc


NEMOTRON_RESPONSE_FORMAT = {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
        "name": "OrderFields",
        "schema": {
            "properties": {
                "order_id": {
                    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
                    "description": "Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated",
                    "title": "Order Id",
                },
                "customer_name": {
                    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
                    "description": "Full name of the customer as written",
                    "title": "Customer Name",
                },
                "customer_email": {
                    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
                    "description": "Customer's email address",
                    "title": "Customer Email",
                },
                "order_date": {
                    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
                    "description": "Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated",
                    "title": "Order Date",
                },
                "total_amount": {
                    "anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "null"}],
                    "description": "Order total as a plain number, no symbol",
                    "title": "Total Amount",
                },
                "currency": {
                    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
                    "description": "ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR",
                    "title": "Currency",
                },
                "issue": {
                    "enum": [
                        "damaged",
                        "missing_item",
                        "wrong_item",
                        "late_delivery",
                        "billing_error",
                        "other",
                    ],
                    "title": "Issue",
                    "type": "string",
                },
            },
            "required": [
                "order_id",
                "customer_name",
                "customer_email",
                "order_date",
                "total_amount",
                "currency",
                "issue",
            ],
            "title": "OrderFields",
            "type": "object",
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
        "strict": True,
    },
}


def extract_order(client: Anthropic, email: str) -> OrderFields:
    response = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
        max_tokens=1024,
        system=EXTRACT_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": f"JSON schema:\n{json.dumps(ORDER_SCHEMA)}\n\nEmail:\n{email}",
            }
        ],
    )
    reply = "".join(block.text for block in response.content if block.type == "text")
    return parse_order_fields(reply)
```

```python
"""Run one HelpHub workflow against a case from a fixtures file.

    python -m helphub.cli triage tests/fixtures/tickets.json --id tkt-1001
    python -m helphub.cli extract tests/fixtures/emails/001-damaged-mug.eml
    python -m helphub.cli search "how do I reset my password"

Needs OPENAI_API_KEY and/or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from anthropic import Anthropic
from openai import OpenAI

from helphub.inbox.triage import triage_ticket
from helphub.kb import Article, load_articles
from helphub.models import ThreadMessage, ToolResult
from helphub.offramp_client import token_factory_client
from helphub.ops.agent_step import next_action
from helphub.orders.extract import extract_order
from helphub.qa.rag_answer import answer_question
from helphub.refunds.plan import RefundRequest, plan_refund
from helphub.search.embed import search_kb
from helphub.summaries.summarize import summarize_thread

# command -> runner taking one fixture case (a dict) and returning something JSON-serialisable
COMMANDS = {
    "triage": lambda c: triage_ticket(token_factory_client(), c["subject"], c["body"]),
    "next-step": lambda c: next_action(
        Anthropic(), c["ticket_text"], [ToolResult(**h) for h in c["history"]]
    ).model_dump(),
    "answer": lambda c: answer_question(
        OpenAI(), c["question"], [Article(**s) for s in c["snippets"]]
    ).model_dump(),
    "refund": lambda c: plan_refund(OpenAI(), RefundRequest(**c)).model_dump(),
    "summarize": lambda c: summarize_thread(
        Anthropic(), [ThreadMessage(**m) for m in c["messages"]]
    ),
}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="helphub", description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in COMMANDS:
        sub = commands.add_parser(name)
        sub.add_argument("fixtures", type=Path, help="JSON file holding a list of cases")
        sub.add_argument("--id", required=True, help="id of the case to run")
    commands.add_parser("extract").add_argument("email", type=Path, help="email as a text file")
    commands.add_parser("search").add_argument("query")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.command == "search":
        hits = search_kb(OpenAI(), args.query, load_articles())
        result = [{"id": a.id, "title": a.title} for a in hits]
    elif args.command == "extract":
        result = extract_order(Anthropic(), args.email.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).model_dump()
    else:
        cases = json.loads(args.fixtures.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        case = next((c for c in cases if c["id"] == args.id), None)
        if case is None:
            print(f"no case {args.id!r} in {args.fixtures}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        result = COMMANDS[args.command](case)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```python
"""Pins the shape of HelpHub's LLM call sites.

The demo is a target for Offramp's AST scanner, so each call site must stay a direct
`client.<api>.create(...)` call with literal keyword arguments, exactly one per file, with its
prompt held in a module-level constant. These tests fail if a refactor hides a call site.
"""

import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

PACKAGE = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "helphub"
API_CHAINS = {
    ("chat", "completions", "create"): "chat",
    ("messages", "create"): "chat",
    ("embeddings", "create"): "embeddings",
}

# file -> (model, module-level constant holding the prompt)
CHAT_SITES = {
    "inbox/triage.py": ("nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning", "TRIAGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT"),  # cs_01
    "ops/agent_step.py": ("claude-sonnet-4-5", "AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT"),  # cs_02
    "orders/extract.py": ("claude-sonnet-4-5", "EXTRACT_SYSTEM_PROMPT"),  # cs_03
    "qa/rag_answer.py": ("gpt-4o", "RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT"),  # cs_04
    "refunds/plan.py": ("o3", "REFUND_POLICY"),  # cs_05
    "summaries/summarize.py": ("claude-haiku-4-5", "SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT"),  # cs_06
}


def attribute_chain(node: ast.expr) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    names = []
    while isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
        names.append(node.attr)
        node = node.value
    return tuple(reversed(names))


def llm_calls(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, ast.Call]]:
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    found = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            chain = attribute_chain(node.func)
            for suffix, kind in API_CHAINS.items():
                if chain[-len(suffix) :] == suffix:
                    found.append((kind, node))
    return found


def module_constants(path: Path) -> dict[str, ast.expr]:
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return {
        node.targets[0].id: node.value
        for node in tree.body
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
    }


def keywords(call: ast.Call) -> dict[str, ast.expr]:
    assert not call.args, "call sites use keyword arguments only"
    assert all(k.arg for k in call.keywords), "no **kwargs unpacking at a call site"
    return {k.arg: k.value for k in call.keywords}


def test_there_are_exactly_these_llm_calls():
    per_file = {
        str(p.relative_to(PACKAGE)): [kind for kind, _ in llm_calls(p)]
        for p in sorted(PACKAGE.rglob("*.py"))
    }
    found = {path: kinds for path, kinds in per_file.items() if kinds}

    assert found == {**{path: ["chat"] for path in CHAT_SITES}, "search/embed.py": ["embeddings"]}


def test_chat_sites_sort_into_the_documented_scan_order():
    assert list(CHAT_SITES) == sorted(CHAT_SITES)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("relative", CHAT_SITES)
def test_chat_site_uses_a_literal_model_and_a_module_level_prompt(relative):
    model, prompt = CHAT_SITES[relative]
    path = PACKAGE / relative
    ((_, call),) = llm_calls(path)
    kwargs = keywords(call)

    assert isinstance(kwargs["model"], ast.Constant) and kwargs["model"].value == model
    assert isinstance(module_constants(path)[prompt], ast.Constant)
    assert prompt in ast.unparse(call)
    assert any(isinstance(n, ast.JoinedStr) for n in ast.walk(call)), "user message is an f-string"


def test_openai_reasoning_site_follows_the_o3_parameter_rules():
    ((_, call),) = llm_calls(PACKAGE / "refunds/plan.py")
    kwargs = keywords(call)

    assert "max_completion_tokens" in kwargs
    assert "temperature" not in kwargs and "max_tokens" not in kwargs


def test_tool_use_site_passes_a_module_level_tools_list():
    path = PACKAGE / "ops/agent_step.py"
    ((_, call),) = llm_calls(path)

    assert isinstance(keywords(call)["tools"], ast.Name)
    assert isinstance(module_constants(path)["TOOLS"], ast.List)


def test_json_extraction_site_builds_its_schema_from_a_pydantic_model():
    path = PACKAGE / "orders/extract.py"

    assert ast.unparse(module_constants(path)["ORDER_SCHEMA"]) == "OrderFields.model_json_schema()"
    ((_, call),) = llm_calls(path)
    assert "ORDER_SCHEMA" in ast.unparse(call)
```

```python
"""Offline stand-ins for the OpenAI and Anthropic clients, plus the fixture loader.

The fakes return real SDK response objects and reject keyword arguments the real SDK
method does not accept, so a typo in a call site fails here rather than in production.
Nothing in the test suite touches the network.
"""

import inspect
import json
import re
import zlib
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

from anthropic.resources.messages import Messages
from anthropic.types import Message, TextBlock, ToolUseBlock, Usage
from openai.resources.chat.completions import Completions
from openai.resources.embeddings import Embeddings
from openai.types import CreateEmbeddingResponse
from openai.types.chat import ChatCompletion

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"


def load_cases(name: str) -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads((FIXTURES / f"{name}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def case_ids(cases: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    return [c["id"] for c in cases]


def _check_kwargs(method, kwargs: dict) -> None:
    unknown = set(kwargs) - set(inspect.signature(method).parameters)
    assert not unknown, f"{method.__qualname__} does not accept {sorted(unknown)}"


def chat_completion(text: str | None) -> ChatCompletion:
    return ChatCompletion.model_validate(
        {
            "id": "chatcmpl-fake",
            "object": "chat.completion",
            "created": 0,
            "model": "fake",
            "choices": [
                {
                    "index": 0,
                    "finish_reason": "stop",
                    "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                }
            ],
        }
    )


def word_vector(text: str, dims: int = 512) -> list[float]:
    """Deterministic bag-of-words embedding: similar wording gives similar vectors."""
    vec = [0.0] * dims
    for word in re.findall(r"\w+", text.lower()):
        vec[zlib.crc32(word.encode()) % dims] += 1.0
    return vec


class FakeOpenAI:
    """Replies to chat completions with `reply`; embeddings come from `embed`."""

    def __init__(self, reply: str | None = "", embed: Callable[[str], list[float]] = word_vector):
        self.reply, self.embed = reply, embed
        self.calls: list[dict] = []
```

```python
import json
from typing import Literal

from anthropic import Anthropic
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError


class OrderFields(BaseModel):
    order_id: str | None = Field(description="Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated")
    customer_name: str | None = Field(description="Full name of the customer as written")
    customer_email: str | None = Field(description="Customer's email address")
    order_date: str | None = Field(description="Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated")
    total_amount: float | None = Field(description="Order total as a plain number, no symbol")
    currency: str | None = Field(description="ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR")
    issue: Literal[
        "damaged", "missing_item", "wrong_item", "late_delivery", "billing_error", "other"
    ]


ORDER_SCHEMA = OrderFields.model_json_schema()

EXTRACT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You extract structured order data from customer support emails.
Reply with a single JSON object that validates against the JSON schema given in the user message.
Use null for any field the email does not state; never guess.
Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD, currencies as ISO 4217 codes, and amounts as plain numbers with a dot
as the decimal separator. Keep names exactly as written. The email may be in any language.
Do not wrap the JSON in markdown and do not add any commentary."""

    """The model's reply was not a JSON object matching `OrderFields`."""
```
